requirement: Embed an arbitrary number of documents with the OpenAI embeddings endpoint while respecting a per-request batch limit and returning vectors aligned with the input.
skeleton: An EmbeddingCountError and embed_all validating batch_size and blank texts, slicing batches, calling client.embeddings.create, sorting data by index, and checking the count per batch.
caption: Embedding a list of texts through an OpenAI client in batches. embed_all(client, texts, *, model, batch_size=100) raises ValueError saying batch_size must be positive when it is below 1, and ValueError saying texts must be non-empty when any text is blank after stripping, both before any request. It slices texts into consecutive batches of batch_size and calls client.embeddings.create with the model and the batch as input. The response data items are sorted by their index field because the API does not promise order; a count different from the batch size raises EmbeddingCountError, a RuntimeError. Embeddings are appended so the result lines up with texts. The fixture asserts that seven texts go out as batches of 3, 3 and 1 with the model name, that vectors follow input order although the fake returns them reversed, that empty input makes no call, that a whitespace text and batch_size 0 raise ValueError, and that a short response raises EmbeddingCountError.

constraints: Blank texts raise ValueError before any request
Texts are sent in consecutive batches of at most batch_size
Response items are ordered by their index field

rationale.teaches: Batch requests to the provider limit and realign results by the returned index so each vector maps back to its text.
rationale.why: Trusting response order silently attaches vectors to the wrong documents, and off-by-one slicing drops the tail of the corpus.

ops.docstring: Embed many texts through an OpenAI client in ordered, bounded batches.

ops.source:
class EmbeddingCountError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when a batch returns a different number of embeddings."""

candidates.why_wrong: Vectors are attached in response order, mismatching documents and embeddings.
The final batch is never sent, dropping the tail of the input.
A short response silently misaligns every following vector.
Whitespace-only texts are sent to the API instead of being rejected.
A batch size of zero is accepted and fails later inside range.
